  {pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b002}
There is a constant $C>0$ such that, for every dimension $n$ and every function
$f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ with $0\le f(x)\le1$ for all $x$, the following holds. If
$0<\varepsilon\le e^{-2}$ and every coordinate's noisy influence at parameter
$1-1/\log(1/\varepsilon)$ is at most $\varepsilon$, then for every $0<\rho<1$,
$\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)\le H_\rho(\mathbb E
f)+\frac{C\log\log(1/\varepsilon)}{(1-\rho)\log(1/\varepsilon)}$, where $H_\rho(\alpha)$
denotes the Gaussian halfspace stability at correlation $\rho$ and volume $\alpha$.
\end{theorem}

  {BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.instIsProbabilityMeasureRealStandardGaussianMeasure_8}
  {context}
  {mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}
  {pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b002}
There is a constant $C>0$ such that, for every dimension $n$ and every function
$f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ with $0\le f(x)\le1$ for all $x$, the following holds. If
$0<\varepsilon\le e^{-2}$ and the maximum absolute coordinate influence of $f$ is at
most $\varepsilon$, then for every $0<\rho<1$, $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)\le
H_\rho(\mathbb E f)+\frac{C\log\log(1/\varepsilon)}{(1-\rho)\log(1/\varepsilon)}$, where
$H_\rho(\alpha)$ denotes the Gaussian halfspace stability at correlation $\rho$ and
volume $\alpha$.
\end{theorem}
